reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes purchasing BitClub founder pools as a passive-income mining investment, presenting a $3,500 purchase as producing $6,212 in nine months and suggesting continued long-term Bitcoin income. It also encourages participation through a team and level structure, with higher income associated with attracting partners, rather than merely reporting on or criticizing the offer.

citations.quote: Lazy account with passive income in BitClub Network
BitClub Network - Marketing bitclub Join the team of leaders
invested into the purchase of a founder pool for $ 3,500. And now we can see exactly how much these founder pools mined
in nine months this account gave us six thousand two hundred twelve dollars
the income there may show a hundred times or even 1000 times more money

opening.argument: Judge this as investment commentary, not a promise of returns. The speaker explicitly allows for a decline before any further rise: “it'll possibly go down then grow again.” He also says the dollar figures depend on the Bitcoin price, which had changed since his earlier review. Those qualifications matter: a calculation at a particular market price is not a guaranteed future payout. The account example may be optimistic, but optimism alone does not establish that viewers are being promised the same result.

citations.quote: course, I think it'll grow further, of course it'll possibly go down then grow again
now of course already another situation, since the rate has changed since that time
in nine months this account gave us six thousand two hundred twelve dollars

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited $3,500 purchase and nine-month dollar figure describe one account, not a stated guarantee to viewers. The opening also treats the team language as decisive, but a call to join a team does not by itself establish what any viewer would earn. The speaker's own concession that the value could fall limits the force of the projected-income reading.

citations.quote: in nine months this account gave us six thousand two hundred twelve dollars
Join the team of leaders
it'll possibly go down then grow again

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A brief acknowledgment of price volatility does not undo the pitch. The speaker presents a paid founder-pool purchase as yielding $6,212 in nine months, then tells viewers the investment will continue producing Bitcoin income. The description directly invites people to join the team. Those elements make the video promotional even without an absolute guarantee.

citations.quote: invested into the purchase of a founder pool for $ 3,500
in nine months this account gave us six thousand two hundred twelve dollars
you will continue receiving interest in Bitcoins
Join the team of leaders

opening.argument: The substance of the video is an account walkthrough. The speaker introduces it as another review of an investment account, checks the date of its first funding, examines the pools, and works through their figures with a calculator. That sequence gives the judge a concrete reason to read the dollar total as an illustration of how this account is being evaluated, not proof that the same result is offered to every viewer. Even the demonstrated figures remain account-specific.

citations.quote: Today I will do another review on my investment account in BitClub
First filing happened on March, 06, 2017 and today we have December, 06, 2017.
let's just count how much profit brought brought all these pools together, for this I will open the calculator

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening cites the purchase and the calculated nine-month total, but those are precisely the inputs the speaker walks through; showing a calculation is not the same as guaranteeing a viewer's outcome. The description's invitation is promotional context, yet it does not erase the video's detailed examination of an existing account and its pool figures.

citations.quote: for this I will open the calculator and let's just add these indicators
Join the team of leaders

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can still sell the arrangement it demonstrates. Here the speaker connects the founder-pool purchase to a large claimed return, suggests the income will continue, and closes by contrasting it with the still greater income available through another level. The account screens support that this is a demonstration, but they do not make its promotional claims merely instructional.

citations.quote: in nine months this account gave us six thousand two hundred twelve dollars
you will continue receiving interest in Bitcoins
there will be another level, the income there may show a hundred times or even 1000 times more money

opening.argument: The concrete transaction described is a purchase of founder-pool shares, followed by an account display of mining figures. The speaker even says this account did not attract partners, so its presented result is not attributed to a downline. The record does show a team invitation, but that alone does not show a requirement to recruit, a guaranteed payout, or a request for viewers' credentials. On this evidence, the judge can distinguish promotion of a paid service from proof of a deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: invested into the purchase of a founder pool for $ 3,500. And now we can see exactly how much these founder pools mined
Let's make sure that this user hasn't attracted any partners
Join the team of leaders

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening is right that the speaker promotes a paid pool and discusses higher levels. But its cited account result is expressly presented without recruited partners; the level comparison does not establish that recruiting produced this account's displayed mining figures. A promotional invitation is not, by itself, evidence of a guaranteed return or a compulsory downline.

citations.quote: Let's make sure that this user hasn't attracted any partners
there will be another level, the income there may show a hundred times or even 1000 times more money
Join the team of leaders

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of recruited partners on this example does not make the offer ordinary commerce. The video presents a $3,500 founder-pool purchase as producing mining income, projects continued Bitcoin interest, and points to much greater income at another level. The accompanying team invitation reinforces the solicitation. None of that requires a credential request or an explicit guarantee to be concerning.
